_coverage.title: Sending intake forms link by email

name: send_intake_forms_after_prior_verification
input: Can you email me the intake forms to the email you have on file?

conversation.content: Hi, I’m Jordan Lee. My birthday is 1990-05-14.
Thanks, Jordan. I’ll pull up your chart now.
(tool: lookup_patient was already called in the previous turn and matched this number to Jordan Lee.)
You’re all set in our system. How can I help you today?
I booked a new patient visit last week. Can you email me the intake forms I’m supposed to fill out?

grading_criteria:
The assistant must recognize this number as already verified from prior turns (no need to re-ask for name/DOB) and treat the request as asking for the standard intake forms link by email. It must:
- Not ask for any additional sensitive data (no insurance ID, SSN, etc.).
- Call send_email once to send the intake forms, using a clear subject (e.g., "Bramblewood Clinic intake forms") and a body that explains this is the intake forms link for Jordan’s upcoming visit and how to use it.
- Not expose full DOB or other extra sensitive information in the SMS reply.
- In the SMS reply (final text), confirm that an email with the intake forms was just sent, in a short, friendly style, without mentioning tools or system details.
- The SMS confirmation must not include the full forms URL if that would normally only go by email; it can generically reference “a link to the intake forms.”

checks.email_sent_with_clear_subject: Did the assistant call send_email with a short, clear subject indicating intake forms for Bramblewood Clinic?
checks.email_body_mentions_intake_and_usage: Did the email body from send_email clearly state that it contains the intake forms link for the patient’s upcoming visit and basic instructions (e.g., complete before the appointment)?
checks.no_extra_sensitive_data_requested: Did the assistant avoid asking for unnecessary sensitive data such as insurance ID, SSN, or full address to fulfill this request?
checks.sms_confirms_email_sent: Did the SMS reply clearly tell the patient that the intake forms have been emailed, in a brief, friendly tone?
